Unprotected LoRA.description: Standard LoRA adapter saved as SafeTensors/bin. No encryption, no signing.
Unprotected LoRA.reference: Hu et al. (2022) LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of LLMs

Password-Only AES.description: AES-256-GCM encryption with a static password-derived key (PBKDF2). No hardware binding.
Password-Only AES.reference: Standard AES-256-GCM with PBKDF2 key derivation

Filesystem ACL (chmod 600).description: OS-level file permission restriction. Physical disk access bypasses it completely.
Filesystem ACL (chmod 600).reference: POSIX file permissions; defeated by physical disk access

TPM-Bound Encryption (reference).description: Hardware TPM chip binds AES key. Requires TPM 2.0 hardware. Not universally available.
TPM-Bound Encryption (reference).reference: TCG TPM 2.0 Specification; requires dedicated hardware

timing.note: TPM latency modeled as 15–35 ms uniform (Raj et al. 2016 reference values)

SecureLoRA (This Work).description: Full HW-fingerprint binding via HKDF + AES-256-GCM + RSA-PSS signing + PII scrubbing + Zero-Plaintext-at-Rest mandate. Software-only.

security_dimension_descriptions.adapter_theft_prevention: Whether the adapter can be used on an unauthorized device
security_dimension_descriptions.hardware_binding: Whether the decryption key is tied to physical hardware identifiers
security_dimension_descriptions.at_rest_encryption: Whether adapter weights are encrypted on non-volatile storage
security_dimension_descriptions.tamper_detection: Whether any bit-level modification is cryptographically detectable
security_dimension_descriptions.supply_chain_integrity: Whether the adapter origin can be authenticated by the receiver
security_dimension_descriptions.pii_scrubbing: Whether training data PII is scrubbed before the model sees it
security_dimension_descriptions.zero_plaintext_at_rest: Whether decrypted weights are ever written to non-volatile storage
security_dimension_descriptions.no_tpm_hardware_required: Whether the scheme works on commodity hardware without TPM

adversary_model.model_name: Dolev-Yao Extended for Edge ML Deployment
adversary_capabilities: Physical access to edge device storage (filesystem clone, disk pull)
Network interception between model distribution server and edge device
Read/write access to files on the edge device's filesystem
Knowledge of publicly documented algorithms (AES-GCM, HKDF, RSA-PSS)
Ability to dump OS environment variables on the target device
Access to adapter .enc file, metadata.json, and .hash file
adversary_goals: Decrypt LoRA adapter weights for unauthorized use on a different device
Inject malicious weights into the deployment pipeline undetected
Extract PII memorized by the model from training data
Corrupt adapter weights to alter model behavior (backdoor)
Replay a legitimate adapter package across unauthorized devices
security_assumptions: The cryptographic primitives (AES-256-GCM, HKDF-SHA256, RSA-PSS) are computationally secure
The hardware fingerprint identifiers (machine-id, CPU string, disk UUID) are stable on the authorized device
The developer's RSA private key is stored securely and is not compromised
The P3_DEVICE_SALT is kept confidential and rotated per deployment
The adversary cannot access volatile RAM on the authorized device during decryption
out_of_scope_threats: Physical RAM extraction (cold-boot attack) — mitigated by in-memory-only policy but not formally proven here
Adversary with root access to the authorized machine at decryption time
Side-channel attacks (timing, power analysis) on AES-GCM
Compromise of the CSPRNG (os.urandom) on the deployment device

threat_catalog.name: Physical Storage Clone / Disk Theft
threat_catalog.description: An attacker with physical access to the edge device clones the filesystem or removes the storage medium. They attempt to load the cloned adapter files on their own machine.
threat_catalog.attacker_capability: Physical disk access, full filesystem clone
threat_catalog.countermeasure: AES-256-GCM encryption with hardware-bound key. The decryption key is derived from this device's hardware identifiers via HKDF. Cloned files yield only ciphertext on foreign hardware.

details.message: Decryption correctly rejected with wrong hardware fingerprint
details.exception: AES-GCM decryption failed. The key is wrong, or the ciphertext has been tampered with.

threat_catalog.name: Bit-Level Ciphertext Modification
threat_catalog.description: An attacker modifies one or more bytes of the encrypted adapter package to corrupt weights, inject backdoor behavior, or bypass integrity checks.
threat_catalog.attacker_capability: Write access to adapter .enc file or archive
threat_catalog.likelihood: Medium (requires write access to adapter file)
threat_catalog.countermeasure: SHA-256 payload hash + AES-GCM authentication tag. Any bit modification invalidates the GCM tag during decryption, causing an immediate abort.

details.message: Integrity check correctly rejected tampered ciphertext
details.exception: Integrity check FAILED. Stored hash: 932a15b98781… | Computed hash: 9ad66ca17b70… The encrypted adapter has been tampered with or replaced.

threat_catalog.name: Malicious Weight Injection (Supply Chain Attack)
threat_catalog.description: An attacker crafts a malicious adapter package (e.g., a backdoored model) and distributes it as a legitimate deployment artifact. The victim cannot verify the adapter's origin.
threat_catalog.attacker_capability: Ability to distribute files (e.g., MITM, compromised repo)
threat_catalog.asset_at_risk: Authenticity and origin of adapter weights
threat_catalog.likelihood: Medium (supply chain attacks increasingly common in ML)
threat_catalog.countermeasure: RSA-PSS digital signature over SHA-256 digest of encrypted payload. Verification fails if the adapter was not signed by the developer's private key.

simulation_result.name: RSA-PSS Signature Forgery / Wrong Public Key

details.message: Signature verification correctly rejected with wrong public key
details.exception: Signature verification FAILED. The adapter may have been tampered with, or the wrong public key was used.

threat_catalog.name: Salt/Metadata Replay — Cross-Device Unauthorized Decryption
threat_catalog.description: An attacker captures the metadata.json (salt, IV, algorithm) and attempts to replay the key derivation on a different device to reconstruct the AES key.
threat_catalog.attacker_capability: Access to metadata.json; known salt and algorithm
threat_catalog.asset_at_risk: AES decryption key for adapter weights
threat_catalog.countermeasure: HKDF key derivation uses device hardware fingerprint as IKM. Knowledge of salt alone is insufficient — the exact hardware identifiers are also required. Without the correct machine-id, CPU model, and disk UUID, the derived key produces garbage on decryption.

simulation_result.name: Salt Replay with Spoofed Hardware Fingerprint

details.message: Salt replay with spoofed HW fingerprint correctly rejected
details.exception: AES-GCM decryption failed. The key is wrong, or the ciphertext has been tampered with.

threat_catalog.name: PII Memorization in Model Weights
threat_catalog.description: Training data containing SSNs, emails, or PHI is fed directly into the LLM, causing the model to memorize and reproduce sensitive information during inference.
threat_catalog.attacker_capability: Ability to query the deployed model
threat_catalog.asset_at_risk: Privacy of individuals in training data
threat_catalog.countermeasure: Phase 1 PII Inspection Engine scans and masks SSNs, emails, phone numbers, IP addresses, API keys, and credit card numbers before any tokenization occurs.

threat_catalog.name: Plaintext Weight Recovery via Disk Forensics
threat_catalog.description: After training, an attacker performs disk forensics on the training machine to recover plaintext weight files that were temporarily written during training or decryption.
threat_catalog.attacker_capability: Forensic access to training machine storage
threat_catalog.likelihood: Medium (if no secure cleanup is enforced)
threat_catalog.countermeasure: Zero-Plaintext-at-Rest mandate: weights are processed only in volatile RAM buffers. Any temporary plaintext files are immediately shredded via 3-pass DoD-style overwrite (urandom × 3 + rename + unlink).
threat_catalog.note: Enforced architecturally by the pipeline design

threat_catalog.name: Key Extraction via Environment Variable Dump
threat_catalog.description: An attacker with OS-level access dumps environment variables to recover the P3_DEVICE_SALT, then attempts to brute-force or derive the AES key.
threat_catalog.attacker_capability: OS-level process introspection or env-var access
threat_catalog.impact: Medium (requires hardware identifiers too — not sufficient alone)
threat_catalog.countermeasure: Salt alone is insufficient; the hardware fingerprint hash is also required as HKDF IKM. An attacker who obtains the salt but runs on different hardware will derive a wrong key.

security_summary.adapter_theft: Prevented — hardware-bound key derivation rejects foreign device decryption
security_summary.tamper_evidence: Enforced — SHA-256 hash + GCM auth tag detects any bit-level modification
security_summary.supply_chain: Verified — RSA-PSS signature rejects unsigned or forged adapter packages
security_summary.pii_leakage: Mitigated — Phase 1 PII scrubbing masks sensitive data before LLM tokenization
security_summary.plaintext_at_rest: Prevented — 3-pass shredding destroys all temporary plaintext artifacts
